issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably give weight to the applicant's reliance on the consultant's errors, or act outside expertise in commenting on PR eligibility? (Officer's PR comment)
issues.applicant_position: Officer speculated beyond expertise about PR eligibility, ignoring Express Entry changes and his lack of qualifying experience.
issues.result_quote: this in my view would not constitute a sufficiently serious shortcoming to set aside the decision as unreasonable

issues.issue: Was the officer's comment on COVID-19, vaccines and reopening borders, and on applying from abroad, unreasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Returning to India to apply from abroad would be unreasonable, as a work permit there would be hard to obtain.
issues.respondent_position: Comment was obiter, answered the COVID hardship claim, and was reasonable; similar stay cases proceeded despite COVID.
issues.result_quote: I see nothing unreasonable in the comment made by the Officer, which simply noted the improving availability of travel and a vaccine

issues.issue: Was it unreasonable for the officer to expect a new LMIA and refuse the TRP for its absence, given the new argument raised at hearing?
issues.applicant_position: Employer was willing to reapply for an LMIA but had not committed before the TRP decision; officer should not have expected one.
issues.respondent_position: Officer was justified in considering that no second LMIA had been issued; the new argument was not raised in the factum.
issues.result_quote: the Officer’s alternate interpretation, that a new LMIA application would be initiated within a couple months, was also reasonable in the circumstances.

issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably apply a 'compelling reasons' test and fetter discretion under s. 24(1) IRPA?
issues.applicant_position: Section 24(1) requires only that a TRP be justified in the circumstances; the officer wrongly applied a compelling-reasons test and fettered discretion.
issues.result_quote: I am not satisfied that the Applicant has met this burden.

issues.issue: Should the consultant's errors in the three earlier work permit applications have been weighed in the applicant's favour?
issues.applicant_position: Failures were inadvertent and caused by the consultant, so the officer should have assessed that rather than his responsibility.
issues.result_quote: I am not able to provide any precise comment on what exactly was contained in those prior applications, because they were not included in the record.
